title: Introduce cost-radar sampler and quant-attenuator (autoscale econ inspector)
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware cost sampler (cost-radar) and a conservative quantization fallback operator (quant-attenuator). New defaults are non-invasive and gated behind feature flags. Improves unit economics visibility and reduces token-cost spikes from cold/micro-burst traffic.
description:
Context and motivation: production traffic exhibits transient micro-bursts and tenant coldstart patterns that inflate per-token cost when aggressive quant profiles are applied globally. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) cost-radar sampler: a lightweight, tenant-scoped sampler that continuously profiles batch shapes, coldstart frequency, and KV-cache hit patterns; (2) quant-attenuator: a runtime policy agent that applies a conservative quantization fallback for affected tenants during detected cost-surge windows.

Design summary: cost-radar runs as a low-overhead sidecar inside the serving mesh and emits aggregated sketches to the econ inspector. It ships tenant summaries on a 1m cadence (configurable) and triggers a policy decision when the sampled unit-econ delta exceeds a threshold. The quant-attenuator translates policy decisions into guarded runtime actions: temporarily switch to a compatible, higher-precision profile (e.g., q4 -> q8 fallback) for the tenant's warmup lane, optionally increase batch sizing and invoke a short-lived KV-cache prefill. Both components are opt-in by default and controlled by tenant flags and the admin console.

Checklist: - [x] cost-radar sampling prototype implemented (Go) - [x] quant-attenuator policy and runtime hooks (Rust) - [x] telemetry and Grafana dashboard (docs) - [x] unit + integration tests covering policy arbitration - [x] feature-flag gates and rollout plan - [x] CLI dry-run mode for policy simulation

How to test locally: 1) enable feature flag: `redwoodctl flags set tenant:<TENANT> cost_radar=true` 2) run `./dev/local-sampler --tenant <TENANT> --trace` to stream snapshots 3) simulate micro-burst with `tools/simulate_traffic --bursts 50 --shape short` 4) run `redwoodctl econ simulate --dry-run` to validate the quant-attenuator decision without applying changes.

Migration notes: defaults are conservative and opt-in. No automatic tenant-wide quant changes occur until the attenuator policy is enabled for a tenant. Existing autoscale and rollout logic is compatible; tie-breakers when both autoscale and attenuator want to change batch sizing prefer autoscale unless a `force-fallback` flag is set.

Related work: references ENG-9981 (cost signal pipeline), ENG-10012 (tenant warmup strategy), and SUP-2143 (support ticket motivating conservative fallbacks).

review_comments: Diego Ramos (2026-02-16): Nice design. Please add a metric for 'attenuator.decisions' with tenant label so SRE can slice it. Also request adding a unit test for a churny tenant.
Aisha Kaur (2026-02-16): Added metric and a churny-tenant unit test. PTAL.
Markus Feldman (2026-02-18): Question: how does this interact with Dedicated capacity policies? If a tenant is on Dedicated, we should avoid switching quant profiles without ops approval.
Aisha Kaur (2026-02-18): Good catch — added a dedicated_tenant guard in policy.rs; attenuator becomes no-op unless 'allow_dedicated_fallback' is set in tenant settings. Documented in migration notes.
Hannah Lee (2026-02-20): CI flake observed on the sim test; re-ran and green. Approving after minor naming change to metric label.
tests_summary: Unit tests: econ sampler logic, attenuator policy arbitration, KV prefill helper mocks. Integration: simulate_traffic bursts integration (flaky initially, fixed), runtime hook e2e on dev cluster. Perf: micro-benchmark shows 0.8ms median added tail latency for sampler sidecar under 1k qps; cost regression negative (improved) in long-run scenarios.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. Changes are feature-flag gated and conservative by default. Runtime hooks are isolated behind attenuator interface. Main risk: incorrect signal thresholds could cause unnecessary fallbacks — mitigated by CLI dry-run, telemetry dashboards, and staged rollout to 1% tenants.
migration_steps: Roll out cost-radar sampler in staging with flags off; validate telemetry emissions
Enable dry-run mode for attenuator and run `redwoodctl econ simulate` for sampled tenants
Stage enablement to 1% tenant cohort, monitor `attenuator.decisions` and unit-econ deltas for 48h
Gradually increase rollout to 25% then 100% with ops approval
If adverse regressions observed, use `redwoodctl flags set all cost_attenuator=false` to disable globally
